title: Diagnosis and Repair of a Leaking Water Heater: T&P Valve, High Pressure, and Expansion Tank

locations.name: Main water supply entry to the building (near the water heater) showing the point where the city supply is split to irrigation and the house
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly identifies the water main coming in from the street and a split to two meters; the equipment is shown around the heater area, suggesting the main feed location is in the same vicinity.

summary: This instructional video analyzes a leaking water heater scenario by tracing upstream causes to high incoming water pressure and insufficient expansion accommodation in a closed hot-water system. The hosts identify the T&P (temperature and pressure) relief valve as the leak point and diagnose excessive pressure arising from a city supply that previously fed a pressure-reducing valve (PRV) installed for irrigation. They explain how a PRV can behave like a check valve, potentially preventing expansion from dissipating in the system and driving pressure back toward the heater. The solution demonstrated is installing a potable water expansion tank to provide a dedicated expansion cavity, paired with push-fit fittings for a leak-tolerant install. The segment emphasizes safe handling of the T&P valve, the relationship between service pressure and appliance longevity, and the concrete steps to add an expansion tank to a domestic potable water system.

sections.title: Identify T&P valve and leakage behavior
sections.description: Introduction to the temperature and pressure relief valve, its safety role, and proper drainage behavior when a leak is observed.

sections.title: High city pressure and PRV role
sections.description: Observation of elevated incoming pressure via a gauge on the outdoor irrigation line and discussion of how a pressure-reducing valve reduces that pressure for household use, with implications for wear and leakage.

sections.title: PRV as check valve and directional flow
sections.description: Explanation that the PRV functions as a check valve, allowing flow in only one direction and potentially influencing where expansion pressure can relieve, which may contribute to the T&P valve issue.

sections.title: Thermal expansion, dip tube, and system balance
sections.description: Discussion of how heated water expands, the role of the dip tube in delivering cold water to the bottom, and the necessity of a proper expansion path to prevent pressure buildup.

sections.title: Install potable water expansion tank
sections.description: Proposal to install a potable water expansion tank to provide a dedicated expansion reservoir and to address the observed overpressure without compromising potable water safety.

sections.title: Repair completion and testing
sections.description: Final installation steps for the potable expansion tank using push-fit connections, refilling the system, and confirming the absence of leaks.
